text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's government, facing an AIDS epidemic which is killing at least 300 people each week, said it had no money to import protease inhibitors which, when used together with other anti-AIDS drugs, have wiped out symptoms of the killer disease.

- State-owned Air Zimbabwe is to set aside a special plane for use by President Robert Mugabe during his foreign visits to eliminate flight disruptions that have hounded the airline in the last few months, an official said last week.

- The International Crops Research Institute for Semi-Arid Tropics, with its regional headquarters in Zimbabwe's southern city of Bulawayo, says it is short of cash and has been forced to scale down its operations.

- The former general manager of the state-owned Grain Marketing Board, Renson Gasela, has established an agri-business company, which is introducing a new system likely to revolutionalise the storage of various agricultural commodities in the country.
- Zimbabwe's government has opened up the under-capitalised Small Enterprises Development Corporation to other players to inject badly-needed fresh funds and boost the corporation's operations.
- The Zimbabwe government has finally decided to build the new Harare International Airport after putting off the exercise since independence from Britain in 1980.
- The Ministry of Education has warned headmasters against increasing school fees and levies without first seeking its permission.
